messages:
From: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@finservcorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finservcorp.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: up-to-date processing partner roster + attestation

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. As part of our vendor intake checklist we need the latest list of third-party processing partners (anyone that processes or routes customer data for Redwood) and a short attestation confirming:

- Whether those processors handle data in the EU/UK or other restricted jurisdictions,
- Which processors (if any) perform encryption or KMS/HSM key management, and
- Confirmation that Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II coverage and whether any processors are covered within that scope.

Could you also flag any entries that are temporary (<=90 days) or in pilot? We need the roster and attestation by COB Apr 7 to keep the procurement review on schedule.

Appreciate it — Claire

Claire Thompson
Vendor Risk Manager
FinServCorp

Attachments: none

Notes:
- We already have a master subprocessors CSV in //internal/shared/privacy/rosters but it was updated last month; Claire explicitly asked for temporary/pilot flags and KMS/HSM indication which may not be in the public column set.

Thanks — Jordan

Claire / team — attaching a redlined roster export and a draft attestation template. Quick summary of what I changed:

- Added pilot_flag entries for two transient telemetry agents (EdgeProbe, PilotFlow) and set expected sunset dates in the notes column.
- Explicitly annotated residency for EU-handling vendors (EdgeStream EU, CacheGrid-EU) and added a residency_note linking to our cross-border transfer SOP.
- Added a KMS column and marked internal HSM usage vs. vendor-managed KMS for the small set of encryption processors.

Draft attestation: "Redwood Inference attests that, to the best of its knowledge and consistent with contractual obligations, the processing partners listed in subprocessors_roster_v3.csv (and annexes) handle customer data in the jurisdictions indicated; vendors responsible for key management are called out in the KMS column. Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II coverage; vendor inclusions within scope are indicated in the \"SOC2_scope\" column. Temporary/pilot vendors are flagged where applicable."

Kimberly — I left several unresolved items in the "SOC2_scope" column (marked TODO) where we need your confirmation about inclusion in the current audit scope. Also, Claire asked for KMS/HSM vendors to be enumerated — I added a short list but would appreciate a verification.

Uploading: subprocessors_roster_v3.csv (attached, redlined)
Uploading: redwood_attestation_finserv.docx (draft attestation)

Action items:
- Kimberly: confirm SOC2 scope flags and validate KMS vendor list (by Apr 6 EOD).
- Jordan: if you want an exec-signed corporate letter, say so — I can convert the attestation to a letterhead doc and route for signature.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: subprocessors_roster_v3.csv, redwood_attestation_finserv.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: up-to-date processing partner roster + attestation

Claire / all — quick clarifications below after reviewing the roster:

- SOC2 scope: EdgeStream EU, CacheGrid-EU, TelemetryHub (on-prem partner) are included in our latest Type II scope; other monitoring/analytics vendors are assessed but not in-scope. I updated the SOC2_scope column in the attached CSV (see values TRUE/FALSE).
- KMS/HSM: Redwood uses a combination of customer-managed keys (HSM-backed) for Dedicated deployments and vendor-managed KMS for some telemetry vendors. Explicit vendors that touch keys: KeyFort (HSM provider, used for on-prem HSM appliances), CloudKeys (vendor KMS used by our hosted telemetry ingest), and Internal-KMS (Redwood-managed, HSM-backed, not a third-party). I added these three entries to the KMS column and a short note on whether key material resides in-custody or vendor-custody.
- Temporary vendors: EdgeProbe and PilotFlow remain flagged as temporary (sunset 2027-07-01).

Claire — if you need a formal attestation signed by our CISO, Jordan, Marissa — I recommend the signed letter. Marissa, please prep on letterhead; Jordan can confirm signature route.

Kimberly

Attachments: subprocessors_roster_v3.csv (updated)
From: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@finservcorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 15:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: up-to-date processing partner roster + attestation

Thanks everyone — this is perfect and exactly what we needed. A couple of small asks before we close the intake:

1) Can you attach the updated CSV (final) and the attestation as a PDF signed or stamped by your security team? A scanned signature from your CISO is fine.
2) For the KMS entries: please indicate whether the vendor-stored keys are covered by contractual controls (e.g., encryption-in-transit/type, key rotation cadence). A short bullet under each KMS vendor will suffice.

If you can get the signed PDF by EOD Apr 8, we can complete the procurement review and issue the PO.

Best,
Claire

Procurement timeline dependent: Apr 8 deliverable
